  -- canonical unix timestamp numeric (seconds). Use block_timestamp_ts from band_transactions_base when available.
  COALESCE(t."block_timestamp_ts", NULL)        AS block_timestamp,
  -- raw original timestamp string preserved for downstream parsing (if any). Keep original base column casing when selecting.
  t."block_timestamp"                           AS block_timestamp_raw,
  -- canonical numeric amount if present in message_variant or fee; attempt common locations:
  -- 1) If message_variant has an "amount" field numeric, use that.
  -- 2) Else if fee_variant.amount exists (array/object), try first element's amount.
  -- 3) Else NULL.
  COALESCE(
    -- from expanded message_variant (may be a VARIANT with path "amount")
    TRY_TO_NUMBER(m.msg_amount) ,
    -- fee_variant may be object like {"amount":[{"denom":"xxx","amount":"123"}], ...}
    TRY_TO_NUMBER(f.fee_amount)
  )                                             AS amount,
  -- from/to addresses: prefer explicit sender/to fields from transaction/message
  COALESCE(t."sender", m.msg_from)              AS from_address,
  m.msg_to                                      AS to_address,
  -- block number / height
  t."block_height"                              AS block_number
FROM
  CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.TRANSACTIONS AS t

    -- messages variant expanded per-tx: extract common fields from message_variant if present

      txhash                                AS txhash,
      -- normalize some common message_variant paths to scalars using : path access
      -- amount might be a number or an array/object; try several forms
      -- flatten amounts if array present; here we attempt to pull first value as string
      CASE
        WHEN message_variant IS NULL THEN NULL
        WHEN message_variant:"amount" IS NOT NULL THEN
          -- if amount is scalar number or string
          message_variant:"amount"::STRING
        WHEN message_variant:"amounts" IS NOT NULL THEN
          message_variant:"amounts"[0]::STRING
        WHEN message_variant:"value" IS NOT NULL THEN
          message_variant:"value"::STRING
        ELSE NULL
      END                                    AS msg_amount,
      -- common from/to paths
      COALESCE(
        message_variant:"from"::STRING,
        message_variant:"sender"::STRING,
        message_variant:"owner"::STRING
      )                                       AS msg_from,
      COALESCE(
        message_variant:"to"::STRING,
        message_variant:"recipient"::STRING,
        message_variant:"receiver"::STRING
      )                                       AS msg_to
    FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.MESSAGES
  ) AS m
    ON m.txhash = t."txhash"
  LEFT JOIN (
    -- extract fee amount canonical if present in fee_variant
    SELECT
      txhash                                AS txhash,
      CASE
        WHEN fee_variant IS NULL THEN NULL

          CASE
            WHEN IS_ARRAY(fee_variant:"amount") THEN fee_variant:"amount"[0]:"amount"::STRING
            WHEN fee_variant:"amount"::STRING IS NOT NULL THEN fee_variant:"amount"::STRING
            ELSE NULL
          END
        ELSE NULL
      END                                    AS fee_amount
    FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.TRANSACTIONS
  ) AS f
    ON f.txhash = t."txhash"

SELECT
  tx.txhash AS tx_hash,
  tx.block_height AS block_number,
  tx.block_timestamp_ts AS block_timestamp,
  TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(tx.block_timestamp_ts) AS timestamp_iso,
  -- Zilliqa doesn't provide a global tx_index in these tables; use COALESCE of available indexes from message context
  COALESCE(msg.message_field:tx_index::NUMBER, 0) AS tx_index,
  -- sender / from
  COALESCE(msg_from.from_address, tx.sender, NULL) AS from_address,
  -- recipient / to
  COALESCE(msg_to.to_address, msg.message_field:to_address::STRING, NULL) AS to_address,
  -- transfer value normalized to numeric (if present in message_variant)
  TRY_TO_DECIMAL(
    COALESCE(
      msg.message_field:value::STRING,
      msg.message_field:amount::STRING,
      msg.message_field:coins::STRING,
      msg.message_field:amount_value::STRING
    )
  , 38,9) AS value,
  -- canonical transfer type: try to map message_type or message_field:type
  COALESCE(
    msg.message_field:type::STRING,
    msg.message_field:action::STRING,
    CASE
      WHEN msg.message_field:value IS NOT NULL THEN 'transfer'
      WHEN msg.message_field:to_address IS NOT NULL AND msg.message_field:from_address IS NOT NULL THEN 'transfer'
      ELSE 'unknown'
    END
  ) AS transfer_type,
  'band_messages_variant_expanded' AS source_table
FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.band_transactions_base AS tx
JOIN CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.band_messages_variant_expanded AS msg
  ON msg.txhash = tx.txhash
-- Exclude rows that lack confirmation fields: require a non-null block_height and block_timestamp_ts
WHERE tx.block_height IS NOT NULL
  AND tx.block_timestamp_ts IS NOT NULL
  -- Exclude entries present in exceptions table (errors) by comparing txhash or combined identifiers if available.
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.ERRORS e
    WHERE e."tableRow" = tx.txhash
  )

WITH
-- normalize zilliqa transactions (base-table columns quoted; alias to unquoted names)
z_tx AS (
  SELECT
    "hash" AS tx_hash,
    "from" AS from_address,
    "to" AS to_address,
    "timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
    "block_number" AS block_number
  FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ZILLIQA.TRANSACTIONS
),
-- normalize zilliqa transitions (contract/internal transitions)
z_tr AS (
  SELECT
    "hash" AS tx_hash,
    "from" AS from_address,
    "to" AS to_address,
    "timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
    "block_number" AS block_number
  FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ZILLIQA.TRANSITIONS
),
-- unified outgoing events (transactions + transitions) for counting outgoing per address
z_outgoing AS (
  SELECT from_address, to_address, tx_hash, block_timestamp, block_number
  FROM z_tx
  UNION ALL
  SELECT from_address, to_address, tx_hash, block_timestamp, block_number
  FROM z_tr
),
-- count outgoing per address (only confirmed on-chain events: require non-null block_number and block_timestamp)
outgoing_counts AS (
  SELECT
    from_address,
    COUNT(*) AS outgoing_count
  FROM z_outgoing
  WHERE block_number IS NOT NULL
    AND block_timestamp IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY from_address
),
-- step1: all confirmed outgoing from source
hop1 AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM z_outgoing
  WHERE from_address = 'zil1jrpjd8pjuv50cfkfr7eu6yrm3rn5u8rulqhqpz'
    AND block_number IS NOT NULL
    AND block_timestamp IS NOT NULL
),
-- step2: all confirmed outgoing to destination
hop2 AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM z_outgoing
  WHERE to_address = 'zil19nmxkh020jnequql9kvqkf3pkwm0j0spqtd26e'
    AND block_number IS NOT NULL
    AND block_timestamp IS NOT NULL
),
-- candidate 2-hop paths where hop1.to_address = intermediate = hop2.from_address
candidates AS (
  SELECT
    h1.tx_hash AS hop1_tx_hash,
    h1.block_timestamp AS hop1_block_timestamp,
    h1.block_number AS hop1_block_number,
    h1.to_address AS intermediate,
    h2.tx_hash AS hop2_tx_hash,
    h2.block_timestamp AS hop2_block_timestamp,
    h2.block_number AS hop2_block_number
  FROM hop1 h1
  JOIN hop2 h2
    ON h1.to_address = h2.from_address
  WHERE
    h1.tx_hash <> h2.tx_hash
    AND h1.to_address IS NOT NULL
    AND h1.to_address NOT IN ('zil1jrpjd8pjuv50cfkfr7eu6yrm3rn5u8rulqhqpz', 'zil19nmxkh020jnequql9kvqkf3pkwm0j0spqtd26e')
    -- chronological order: hop1 must be earlier than hop2 (compare timestamp then block_number then tx_hash)
    AND (
      h1.block_timestamp < h2.block_timestamp
      OR (
        h1.block_timestamp = h2.block_timestamp
        AND h1.block_number < h2.block_number
      )
      OR (
        h1.block_timestamp = h2.block_timestamp
        AND h1.block_number = h2.block_number
        AND h1.tx_hash < h2.tx_hash
      )
    )
),
-- exclude intermediates with >50 outgoing events
filtered AS (
  SELECT
    c.*,
    COALESCE(oc.outgoing_count, 0) AS intermediate_outgoing
  FROM candidates c
  LEFT JOIN outgoing_counts oc
    ON oc.from_address = c.intermediate
  WHERE COALESCE(oc.outgoing_count, 0) <= 50
)
SELECT
  'zil1jrpjd8pjuv50cfkfr7eu6yrm3rn5u8rulqhqpz --(tx ' || SUBSTR(hop1_tx_hash,1,5) || '..)--> ' ||
    intermediate || ' --(tx ' || SUBSTR(hop2_tx_hash,1,5) || '..)--> zil19nmxkh020jnequql9kvqkf3pkwm0j0spqtd26e'

  hop1_block_timestamp,
  hop1_block_number,

  hop2_tx_hash,
  hop2_block_timestamp,
  hop2_block_number,
  intermediate_outgoing
FROM filtered
ORDER BY hop1_block_timestamp ASC, hop2_block_timestamp ASC

For each request, extract all symbol-rate pairs by matching each symbol in the "symbols" array with its corresponding rate at the same position in the "rates" array from the decoded result. Adjust each rate by dividing it by the request's multiplier value. Return the block timestamp, oracle request ID, symbol, and the adjusted rate for each symbol-rate pair. SELECT
  -- carry key and time columns
  ORACLE_REQUESTS."block_timestamp"             AS block_timestamp,
  ORACLE_REQUESTS."block_height"                AS block_height,
  ORACLE_REQUESTS."oracle_request_id"           AS oracle_request_id,

  -- extract oracle_script.id (path inside VARIANT oracle_script)
  ORACLE_REQUESTS."oracle_script":id::NUMBER    AS oracle_script_id,

  -- extract numeric multiplier from request JSON if present (lift any literal parsing rules out of view)
  -- attempt to read request.params.multiplier or request.multiplier; fallback to NULL
  COALESCE(
    TRY_TO_NUMBER(ORACLE_REQUESTS."request":params:multiplier::STRING),
    TRY_TO_NUMBER(ORACLE_REQUESTS."request":multiplier::STRING)
  )                                             AS request_multiplier,

  -- decoded_result is VARIANT; we expose symbols and rates as ARRAYs.
  -- decoded_result may be object with "symbols" and "rates" arrays or an array of objects; handle common shapes.

  -- decoded_symbols: try decoded_result:symbols, else if decoded_result is array of objects extract symbol fields
  CASE
    WHEN TYPEOF(ORACLE_REQUESTS."decoded_result":symbols) = 'ARRAY' THEN
      ARRAY_AGG(value::STRING) OVER (PARTITION BY ORACLE_REQUESTS."oracle_request_id"
        ORDER BY NULL) -- placeholder; will be replaced by a single-array construction below
    WHEN TYPEOF(ORACLE_REQUESTS."decoded_result") = 'ARRAY' THEN
      -- build array of symbol fields from decoded_result array of objects
      (SELECT ARRAY_AGG(d.value::STRING)
       FROM LATERAL FLATTEN(input => ORACLE_REQUESTS."decoded_result") f,
            LATERAL (SELECT f.value:symbol AS value) d)
    ELSE
      -- try single object with symbols array, or null
      ORACLE_REQUESTS."decoded_result":symbols
  END                                             AS decoded_symbols,

  -- decoded_rates similar handling: try numeric rates array, else extract rates from array of objects
  CASE
    WHEN TYPEOF(ORACLE_REQUESTS."decoded_result":rates) = 'ARRAY' THEN
      ORACLE_REQUESTS."decoded_result":rates
    WHEN TYPEOF(ORACLE_REQUESTS."decoded_result") = 'ARRAY' THEN
      (SELECT ARRAY_AGG(TO_NUMBER(d.value:rate::STRING))
       FROM LATERAL FLATTEN(input => ORACLE_REQUESTS."decoded_result") f,
            LATERAL (SELECT f.value:rate AS value) d)
    ELSE
      ORACLE_REQUESTS."decoded_result":rates
  END                                             AS decoded_rates,

  -- counts: lengths of the arrays where possible
  CASE
    WHEN ORACLE_REQUESTS."decoded_result":symbols IS NOT NULL THEN
      ARRAY_SIZE(ORACLE_REQUESTS."decoded_result":symbols)
    WHEN TYPEOF(ORACLE_REQUESTS."decoded_result") = 'ARRAY' THEN
      (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM LATERAL FLATTEN(input => ORACLE_REQUESTS."decoded_result") )
    ELSE NULL
  END                                             AS symbols_count,

  CASE
    WHEN ORACLE_REQUESTS."decoded_result":rates IS NOT NULL THEN
      ARRAY_SIZE(ORACLE_REQUESTS."decoded_result":rates)
    WHEN TYPEOF(ORACLE_REQUESTS."decoded_result") = 'ARRAY' THEN
      (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM LATERAL FLATTEN(input => ORACLE_REQUESTS."decoded_result") )
    ELSE NULL
  END                                             AS rates_count

FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.ORACLE_REQUESTS AS ORACLE_REQUESTS

subgoals.cte:
SELECT
  oi.id                                                     AS order_item_id,
  oi.order_id                                               AS order_id,
  oi.user_id                                                AS user_id,
  -- keep original product_id and inventory_item_id from order_items
  oi.product_id                                             AS product_id,
  oi.inventory_item_id                                      AS inventory_item_id,
  oi.sale_price                                             AS sale_price,
  -- prefer category from inventory item if present, else from product
  COALESCE(ii.product_category, p.category)                 AS product_category,
  -- resolved product_id: prefer product_id on order_item, else inventory_items.product_id
  COALESCE(oi.product_id, ii.product_id)                    AS product_id_resolved,
  -- prefer cost from inventory item (reflecting item-level cost) else product.cost
  COALESCE(ii.cost, p.cost)                                 AS product_cost,
  -- retail price: prefer inventory item retail price else product.retail_price
  COALESCE(ii.product_retail_price, p.retail_price)         AS product_retail_price,
  -- name/brand/department/sku: prefer inventory item-level fields else product fields
  COALESCE(ii.product_name, p.name)                         AS product_name,
  COALESCE(ii.product_brand, p.brand)                       AS product_brand,
  COALESCE(ii.product_department, p.department)             AS product_department,
  COALESCE(ii.product_sku, p.sku)                           AS product_sku
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS AS oi
LEFT JOIN THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.PRODUCTS AS p
  ON oi.product_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.INVENTORY_ITEMS AS ii
  ON oi.inventory_item_id = ii.id

SELECT
  oi.id AS order_item_id,
  oi.order_id AS order_id,
  -- resolve product_category preference: inventory_items.product_category if present, else products.category
  COALESCE(ii.product_category, p.category) AS product_category,
  -- delivery year/month derived from delivered_at (from order_items if present) -- assume delivered_at is epoch seconds
  DATE_PART(year, TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(oi.delivered_at))::NUMBER AS delivery_year,
  DATE_PART(month, TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(oi.delivered_at))::NUMBER AS delivery_month,
  -- month_start_date as DATE of first day of that month (UTC)
  DATE_TRUNC('month', TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(oi.delivered_at))::DATE AS month_start_date,
  oi.sale_price AS sale_price,
  -- product_cost preference: inventory_items.cost if present, else products.cost
  COALESCE(ii.cost, p.cost) AS product_cost
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS  AS base_oi
  -- follow quoting rules: reference base table columns with exact quoted names, then alias to unquoted names
  , LATERAL (SELECT
      base_oi."id"        AS id,
      base_oi."order_id"  AS order_id,
      base_oi."product_id" AS product_id,
      base_oi."inventory_item_id" AS inventory_item_id,
      base_oi."delivered_at" AS delivered_at,
      base_oi."sale_price" AS sale_price
    ) oi
LEFT JOIN THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.PRODUCTS  AS base_p
  ON base_p."id" = oi.product_id
  , LATERAL (SELECT
      base_p."id"    AS id,
      base_p."cost"  AS cost,
      base_p."category" AS category
    ) p
LEFT JOIN THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.INVENTORY_ITEMS AS base_ii
  ON base_ii."id" = oi.inventory_item_id
  , LATERAL (SELECT
      base_ii."id" AS id,
      base_ii."cost" AS cost,
      base_ii."product_category" AS product_category
    ) ii
-- Only include rows that have a delivered_at (i.e., delivery date) and that are joinable to an order
INNER JOIN THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS AS base_o
  ON base_o."order_id" = oi.order_id
  , LATERAL (SELECT
      base_o."order_id" AS order_id,
      base_o."delivered_at" AS delivered_at
    ) o
WHERE oi.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
  -- ensure there is a resolved category from either inventory or products
  AND (ii.product_category IS NOT NULL OR p.category IS NOT NULL)

WITH order_items AS (
  SELECT
    "id" AS id,
    "order_id" AS order_id,
    "product_id" AS product_id,
    "inventory_item_id" AS inventory_item_id,
    "status" AS status,
    "created_at" AS created_at,
    "shipped_at" AS shipped_at,
    "delivered_at" AS delivered_at,
    "returned_at" AS returned_at,
    "sale_price" AS sale_price
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS
),
orders AS (
  SELECT
    "order_id" AS order_id,
    "user_id" AS user_id,
    "status" AS status,
    "gender" AS gender,
    "created_at" AS created_at,
    "returned_at" AS returned_at,
    "shipped_at" AS shipped_at,
    "delivered_at" AS delivered_at,
    "num_of_item" AS num_of_item
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS
),
products AS (
  SELECT
    "id" AS id,
    "cost" AS cost,
    "category" AS category,
    "name" AS name,
    "brand" AS brand,
    "retail_price" AS retail_price,
    "department" AS department,
    "sku" AS sku,
    "distribution_center_id" AS distribution_center_id
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.PRODUCTS
),
inventory_items AS (
  SELECT
    "id" AS id,
    "product_id" AS product_id,
    "created_at" AS created_at,
    "sold_at" AS sold_at,
    "cost" AS cost,
    "product_category" AS product_category,
    "product_name" AS product_name,
    "product_brand" AS product_brand,
    "product_retail_price" AS product_retail_price,
    "product_department" AS product_department,
    "product_sku" AS product_sku,
    "product_distribution_center_id" AS product_distribution_center_id
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.INVENTORY_ITEMS
),
-- Determine timestamp unit: check typical epoch magnitude by inspecting a sample isn't possible here,
-- assume delivered_at is seconds since epoch as common for these datasets and use cutoff 1640995200.
filtered AS (
  SELECT
    oi.id                                   AS order_item_id,
    oi.order_id                             AS order_id,
    o.delivered_at                          AS delivered_at_ts,
    DATE_TRUNC('month', TO_TIMESTAMP_LTZ(o.delivered_at)) AS month_start,
    EXTRACT(year FROM TO_TIMESTAMP_LTZ(o.delivered_at))  AS delivery_year,
    EXTRACT(month FROM TO_TIMESTAMP_LTZ(o.delivered_at)) AS delivery_month,
    COALESCE(p.category, ii.product_category)            AS product_category,
    COALESCE(oi.sale_price, 0.0)                         AS revenue,
    -- Determine cost: prefer product.cost if available, otherwise inventory item's cost
    COALESCE(p.cost, ii.cost, 0.0)                       AS unit_cost,
    oi.product_id,
    oi.inventory_item_id
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  LEFT JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id
  LEFT JOIN inventory_items ii ON oi.inventory_item_id = ii.id
  WHERE oi.status = 'Complete'
    AND o.status = 'Complete'
    AND o.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
    -- delivered before 2022-01-01 UTC; assuming delivered_at is epoch seconds
    AND o.delivered_at < 1640995200
),
monthly_agg AS (
  SELECT
    month_start,
    delivery_year,
    delivery_month,
    product_category,
    SUM(revenue)                                      AS total_revenue,
    COUNT(DISTINCT order_item_id)                     AS total_completed_orders,
    SUM(unit_cost)                                    AS total_cost
  FROM filtered
  GROUP BY month_start, delivery_year, delivery_month, product_category
),
with_metrics AS (
  SELECT
    month_start,
    delivery_year,
    delivery_month,
    product_category,
    total_revenue,
    total_completed_orders,
    total_cost,
    (total_revenue - total_cost)                                  AS total_profit,
    CASE WHEN total_cost = 0 THEN NULL ELSE (total_revenue - total_cost) / total_cost END AS profit_to_cost_ratio
  FROM monthly_agg
),
with_lag AS (
  SELECT
    wm.*,
    LAG(total_revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY product_category ORDER BY month_start)          AS prev_revenue,
    LAG(total_completed_orders) OVER (PARTITION BY product_category ORDER BY month_start) AS prev_orders
  FROM with_metrics wm
)
SELECT
  product_category,
  delivery_year,
  delivery_month,
  month_start,
  total_revenue,
  total_completed_orders,
  -- month-over-month percentage change (NULL if no previous month or previous = 0)
  CASE WHEN prev_revenue IS NULL OR prev_revenue = 0 THEN NULL ELSE (total_revenue - prev_revenue) / prev_revenue END AS revenue_mom_pct_change,
  CASE WHEN prev_orders IS NULL OR prev_orders = 0 THEN NULL ELSE (total_completed_orders - prev_orders) / prev_orders END AS orders_mom_pct_change,
  total_cost,
  total_profit,
  profit_to_cost_ratio
FROM with_lag
ORDER BY product_category ASC, delivery_year ASC, delivery_month ASC

rows.question: Using data up to the end of 2022 and organized by the month of each user's first purchase, can you provide the percentage of users who made a purchase in each of the first, second, third, and fourth months since their initial purchase, where the "first month" refers to the month of their initial purchase?
rows.rewrite:
Task: For each cohort defined by the calendar month of a user's first purchase (based on orders.created_at) up to and including 2022-12-31, compute the percentage of users in that cohort who made at least one purchase in month 1, month 2, month 3, and month 4 since their initial purchase, where month 1 is the calendar month of the user's first purchase, month 2 is the next calendar month, month 3 is two months after the first purchase month, and month 4 is three months after the first purchase month.
Required outputs: cohort_month (string or YYYY-MM format) — the calendar month of each user's first purchase; cohort_user_count (integer) — number of distinct users whose first purchase month = cohort_month and whose first purchase occurred on or before 2022-12-31; pct_month_1 (float) — percentage (0-100) of cohort users who made at least one purchase in month 1 (the first purchase month); pct_month_2 (float) — percentage (0-100) of cohort users who made at least one purchase in month 2 (the calendar month immediately after the first purchase month); pct_month_3 (float) — percentage (0-100) of cohort users who made at least one purchase in month 3 (two months after the first purchase month); pct_month_4 (float) — percentage (0-100) of cohort users who made at least one purchase in month 4 (three months after the first purchase month)
Filters: Consider only orders with created_at timestamps corresponding to dates on or before 2022-12-31 (inclusive).; Define each user's first purchase as the earliest orders.created_at for that user that is on or before 2022-12-31. Exclude users with no orders on or before 2022-12-31.; Cohort_month is the year-month (YYYY-MM) of that earliest order's created_at (convert created_at epoch/number to date as appropriate).; When determining purchases in months 1–4 for a user, include any orders.created_at that fall within the calendar month windows: month 1 = cohort_month, month 2 = cohort_month + 1 calendar month, month 3 = +2 months, month 4 = +3 months. Only count orders with created_at on or before 2022-12-31.; Count each user at most once per month (presence of >=1 order in that month qualifies the user for that month).
Sort/limit: order results by cohort_month ascending; no row limit

WITH first_orders AS (
  SELECT
    "user_id" AS user_id,
    MIN(DATE_TRUNC('month', TO_TIMESTAMP_LTZ("created_at")))::DATE AS cohort_month
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS
  WHERE "created_at" IS NOT NULL
    AND TO_TIMESTAMP_LTZ("created_at")::DATE <= DATE '2022-12-31'
  GROUP BY "user_id"
),
user_orders AS (
  SELECT
    "user_id" AS user_id,
    DATE_TRUNC('month', TO_TIMESTAMP_LTZ("created_at"))::DATE AS order_month
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS
  WHERE "created_at" IS NOT NULL
    AND TO_TIMESTAMP_LTZ("created_at")::DATE <= DATE '2022-12-31'
),
cohort_activity AS (
  SELECT
    f.user_id,
    f.cohort_month,
    u.order_month,
    DATEDIFF(month, f.cohort_month, u.order_month) AS month_index
  FROM first_orders f
  JOIN user_orders u
    ON f.user_id = u.user_id
),
cohort_months AS (
  SELECT
    cohort_month,
    COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS cohort_size
  FROM first_orders
  GROUP BY cohort_month
),
cohort_retention AS (
  SELECT
    cohort_month,
    month_index,
    COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS users_active
  FROM cohort_activity
  WHERE month_index BETWEEN 0 AND 3
  GROUP BY cohort_month, month_index
),
combined AS (
  SELECT
    cm.cohort_month,
    cr.month_index,
    cr.users_active,
    cm.cohort_size,
    ROUND(100.0 * cr.users_active / cm.cohort_size, 2) AS pct_active
  FROM cohort_months cm
  LEFT JOIN cohort_retention cr
    ON cm.cohort_month = cr.cohort_month
)
SELECT
  cohort_month,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN month_index = 0 THEN pct_active END), 0) AS month_1_pct,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN month_index = 1 THEN pct_active END), 0) AS month_2_pct,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN month_index = 2 THEN pct_active END), 0) AS month_3_pct,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN month_index = 3 THEN pct_active END), 0) AS month_4_pct
FROM combined
GROUP BY cohort_month
ORDER BY cohort_month

rows.question: Based solely on completed orders, calculate the average monthly percentage growth rate in the number of unique orders (counting distinct order IDs) for each product category by comparing each month's count to the previous month within the same category. Identify the product category with the highest average of these monthly order growth rates. Then, for that specific product category, compute the average monthly revenue growth rate by calculating the percentage change in total revenue (sum of sale prices) from month to month and averaging these values over the entire period.
rows.rewrite:
Task: Using only orders that are completed, compute for each product category the month-over-month percentage change in the number of unique orders (distinct order_id) for consecutive calendar months, then compute the average of those monthly percentage changes (i.e., mean of month-to-previous-month percent changes) for each category; identify the category with the highest average monthly order-count growth, and for that single category compute the month-over-month percentage change in total revenue (sum of sale_price across order_items for completed orders) for consecutive calendar months and return the average of those monthly revenue percentage changes over the same time span.
Required outputs: top_category (product category with highest average monthly order-count percentage growth); avg_monthly_order_count_growth_pct (that category's average of month-over-month percent changes in unique order counts, expressed as percentage); avg_monthly_revenue_growth_pct (for that category: average of month-over-month percent changes in total monthly revenue, expressed as percentage); months_used_count (number of month-to-previous-month comparisons used to compute the averages)
Filters: Include only orders with ORDERS.status = 'completed' (case-insensitive match for 'completed').; Aggregate by calendar month derived from the orders' created_at timestamps (use UTC epoch seconds or milliseconds as stored; convert to a Year-Month period, e.g., YYYY-MM).; When counting unique orders per month per product category, count distinct ORDERS.order_id associated with that category via ORDER_ITEMS.product_id -> PRODUCTS.id and PRODUCTS.category.; When computing monthly revenue per category, sum ORDER_ITEMS.sale_price for ORDER_ITEMS belonging to ORDERS with status completed and to products in that category; assign each order_item to the calendar month of its parent ORDERS.created_at.; Only include consecutive months where a previous month exists for that category (i.e., the percent change for the category is computed for months t where month t-1 has at least one order record for that category).; Compute percent change as ((value_month_t - value_month_t-1) / value_month_t-1) * 100. Exclude comparisons where the previous month's value is zero to avoid division by zero; do not impute or drop months beyond that rule.; Use all data available in the database; no external time range filtering unless implied by data.; If multiple categories tie for highest average monthly order-count growth, choose the single category with the highest avg_monthly_order_count_growth_pct by numeric comparison (if still tied, break tie deterministically by lexical order of category name).
rows.plan:
Use the following sources and steps:
- Views/Tables: completed_orders (one row per order, already filtered to completed), ORDER_ITEMS, PRODUCTS.
- Join keys / safety: join completed_orders -> ORDER_ITEMS on order_id (ORDER_ITEMS is one-to-many per order) — re-aggregate ORDER_ITEMS up to order+product category + month before joining into month-level measures to avoid duplication; join ORDER_ITEMS -> PRODUCTS on product_id (one-to-one).
- Projections & time bucketing: derive order_month = strftime('%Y-%m', datetime(completed_orders.created_at, 'unixepoch')) (use UTC epoch seconds). Assign each order_item the parent order_month.
- Per-category, per-month aggregates: for each category and order_month compute (a) unique_order_count = count(distinct completed_orders.order_id) and (b) revenue = sum(order_items.sale_price). To avoid double-counting when an order has multiple items in same category in same month, first collapse at order_id + category + month (keep one row per order-category-month) for unique_order_count, and separately sum sale_price at category+month (summing all order_items assigned).
- Compute month-over-month pct changes: for each category sort by order_month, join each month to previous month (lag) and compute pct_change_orders = ((unique_order_count - prev_unique_order_count)/prev_unique_order_count)*100, excluding cases where prev_unique_order_count = 0; similarly compute pct_change_revenue using revenue and excluding prev revenue = 0.
- Per-category averages: for each category compute avg_monthly_order_count_growth_pct = avg(pct_change_orders) and avg_monthly_revenue_growth_pct = avg(pct_change_revenue) using the same set of month-to-previous-month comparisons; months_used_count = count of comparisons used.
- Pick top category: choose category with highest avg_monthly_order_count_growth_pct (numeric); if tie, pick lexicographically smallest category.
- Output single row: top_category, avg_monthly_order_count_growth_pct, avg_monthly_revenue_growth_pct, months_used_count. Order/limit: return that single row (limit 1).

Joins and keys:
- orders_core JOIN ORDER_ITEMS on orders_core.order_id = ORDER_ITEMS.order_id (orders_core is 1:many; ok because we will aggregate after join).
- LEFT JOIN products_core on ORDER_ITEMS.product_id = products_core.product_id (product-level, 1:1 per product id).
- LEFT JOIN INVENTORY_ITEMS on ORDER_ITEMS.inventory_item_id = INVENTORY_ITEMS.id (inventory item is 1:1 when present).

- month = strftime('%Y-%m', datetime(orders_core.created_at, 'unixepoch')) (or equivalent) for grouping.
- sale_price from ORDER_ITEMS.sale_price summed as total_sales.
- cost per order_item = COALESCE(INVENTORY_ITEMS.cost, products_core.cost) summed as total_cost.
- complete_orders_count = count(DISTINCT orders_core.order_id) but only counting orders that meet filters and have at least one included order_item in the month.
- total_profit = total_sales - total_cost.
- profit_to_cost_ratio = CASE WHEN total_cost = 0 THEN NULL ELSE total_profit / total_cost END.

Filters:
- orders_core.status = 'Complete'
- orders_core.created_at BETWEEN 1672531200 AND 1704067199
- category filter: require COALESCE(products_core.category, INVENTORY_ITEMS.product_category) = 'Sleep & Lounge' — applied in WHERE to include only order_items whose linked product or inventory item is in that category.

Grouping, ordering, limit:
- GROUP BY month
- ORDER BY month ASC
- no LIMIT

- Because ORDER_ITEMS is many-per-order, counting distinct orders ensures complete_orders_count is not inflated.
- Use LEFT JOINs but filter on category (which effectively makes the joins inner for matching items); ensure cost COALESCE picks inventory cost when present.

  WHERE "status" = 'Complete'

products_cte AS (

  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.PRODUCTS
  WHERE "brand" IS NOT NULL
),
joined AS (

  SELECT
    TO_CHAR(DATE_TRUNC('month', TO_TIMESTAMP(oi.created_at)), 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    p.name AS product_name,
    p.brand AS brand,
    p.category AS category,
    oi.id AS order_item_id,

  FROM orders_cte o
  JOIN order_items_cte oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  JOIN products_cte p ON oi.product_id = p.id
  WHERE oi.created_at < 1720204800  -- ensure the order_item's timestamp is also before July 2024
),

  SELECT
    month,
    product_name,
    brand,
    category,

    SUM(sale_price) AS total_revenue_for_tiebreak  -- keep full precision for ordering tie-breaker
  FROM joined
  GROUP BY month, product_name, brand, category

  SELECT
    month,
    product_name,
    brand,
    category,
    total_sales,

rows.question: Can you list the email addresses of the top 10 users who registered in 2019 and made purchases in 2019, ranking them by their highest average order value, where average order value is calculated by multiplying the number of items in each order by the sale price, summing this total across all orders for each user, and then dividing by the total number of orders?

Task: Find the email addresses of the top 10 users (by highest average order value) who both registered in 2019 and placed at least one order in 2019. For each user compute their average order value as: for each order belonging to the user in 2019, compute order_value = num_of_item * (for that order use the sum of sale_price across its order_items? — resolved below as using per-order sum of sale_price from ORDER_ITEMS tied to that order), sum these per-order order_value across all the user's orders in 2019, then divide that sum by the total number of the user's orders in 2019; rank users by this average descending and return the top 10 emails.
Required outputs: email (USERS.email) for each selected user; average_order_value (computed numeric value used for ranking) — optional but recommended for verification
Filters: USERS.created_at must be in calendar year 2019: >= 1546300800 and < 1577836800 (Unix epoch seconds for 2019-01-01 and 2020-01-01); Only consider ORDERS created_at in calendar year 2019: ORDERS.created_at >= 1546300800 and ORDERS.created_at < 1577836800; Join ORDERS to USERS by ORDERS.user_id = USERS.id; When computing per-order monetary value: sum sale_price from ORDER_ITEMS where ORDER_ITEMS.order_id = ORDERS.order_id and ORDER_ITEMS.order_id is in 2019; then multiply that per-order sale_price_sum by ORDERS.num_of_item to produce order_value (if ORDER_ITEMS rows are missing for an order, treat sale_price_sum as 0); Include only users who have at least one ORDERS row in 2019 (by the ORDERS.created_at filter above) and who satisfy the USERS.created_at filter
Sort/limit: Order results by average_order_value DESCENDING and return the top 10 rows
rows.plan:
- Use users_base (one row per user) filtered to USERS.created_at between 1546300800 and 1577836800.
- Use orders_base filtered to ORDERS.created_at between 1546300800 and 1577836800 and joined to users_base on orders_base.user_id = users_base.id (this produces only 2019 orders).
- Use order_item_sums_by_order (one row per order) joined to orders_base on order_item_sums_by_order.order_id = orders_base.order_id to obtain per-order sale_price sums; treat NULL sale sum as 0.
- Compute per-order order_value = COALESCE(order_items_sale_price_sum,0) * orders_base.num_of_item.
- Aggregate per user: SUM(order_value) AS total_order_value_2019 and COUNT(DISTINCT orders_base.order_id) AS orders_count_2019.
- Compute average_order_value = total_order_value_2019 / orders_count_2019; include only users with orders_count_2019 >= 1.
- Project users_base.email and average_order_value.
- Order by average_order_value DESC and LIMIT 10.

rows.question: Please provide the names of the products that had sales in each month of 2020 and had the lowest profit, calculated as the difference between their retail price and cost from the products data. Exclude any months where this data isn't available. Please list the products in chronological order based on the month.
rows.rewrite:
Task: For each calendar month in 2020 (Jan–Dec) find the product(s) that had sales in that month and had the lowest profit among products sold that month, where profit is defined as products.retail_price - products.cost; exclude months with no sales or missing price/cost, and return the product name(s) and the month they correspond to.
Required outputs: month (in YYYY-MM format); product_name (products.name); profit (products.retail_price - products.cost)
Filters: Consider only sales that occurred in 2020: use ORDER_ITEMS.delivered_at or ORDER_ITEMS.created_at (use the table column that records the sale event timestamp available in the schema).; Sale must be associated with a product: ORDER_ITEMS.product_id = PRODUCTS.id.; Include only months where at least one product sold and where PRODUCTS.retail_price IS NOT NULL and PRODUCTS.cost IS NOT NULL.; Profit = PRODUCTS.retail_price - PRODUCTS.cost; exclude rows with NULL profit.; Group sales by calendar month derived from the sale timestamp and year = 2020.; If multiple products tie for the lowest profit in a month, include all tied product names for that month.
Sort/limit: Order results chronologically by month ascending (from 2020-01 to 2020-12); no row limit.
rows.plan:
- Views/tables to use: order_items_with_sale_timestamp (grain: order_items.id), products_basic (grain: products.id).
- Join keys: order_items_with_sale_timestamp.product_id = products_basic.id (many order_items -> one product; safe to join because products_basic is 1-side).
- Projection: month (format YYYY-MM from the sale timestamp), products_basic.name as product_name, products_basic.profit.
- Sale timestamp: use order_items_with_sale_timestamp.delivered_at if present else created_at — rely on the view's canonical sale timestamp column (assume delivered_at is populated there); compute month via DATE or strftime from that timestamp.
- Filters: keep rows where month year = 2020, products_basic.retail_price IS NOT NULL AND products_basic.cost IS NOT NULL AND products_basic.profit IS NOT NULL.
- Aggregation: for each month and product compute that product's profit (products_basic.profit is already product-level, so no aggregation needed per order); determine per-month minimum profit by grouping by month and taking MIN(profit).
- Final join/filter: join per-month min-profit back to product rows to keep only products whose profit = month_min_profit; include ties.
- Ordering/limit: order by month ASC (YYYY-MM) from 2020-01 to 2020-12; no limit.

rows.question: Which three browsers have the shortest average session duration—calculated by the difference in seconds between the earliest and latest timestamps for each user’s session—while only including browsers that have more than 10 total sessions, and what are their respective average session durations?

Task: Compute the three browser names with the smallest (shortest) average session duration, where session duration is defined as, for each session_id, the difference in seconds between the latest and earliest EVENTS.created_at timestamps for that session; only consider sessions that belong to a browser value present in EVENTS.browser, include only browsers that have more than 10 total sessions, and report each browser with its average session duration in seconds.

rows.question: For the user cohort with a first purchase date in January 2020, what proportion of users returned in the subsequent months of 2020?
rows.rewrite:
Task: For users whose first-ever order (first purchase) occurred in January 2020, compute for each subsequent month of 2020 (February through December 2020) the proportion of those users who had at least one returned order in that month. Proportion = (number of cohort users with >=1 returned order in the month) / (total number of users in the cohort).
Required outputs: month (YYYY-MM) - each month from 2020-02 through 2020-12; cohort_size - total number of distinct users whose first order date is in January 2020; users_with_return_in_month - number of distinct cohort users who had one or more orders with returned_at in that month; return_proportion - users_with_return_in_month divided by cohort_size (decimal or percentage)
Filters: Define first purchase date per user as the minimum ORDERS.created_at for that user (epoch or numeric timestamp) converted to a date; cohort includes users where that date is between 2020-01-01 and 2020-01-31 inclusive.; Consider returned orders as orders (ORDERS) with returned_at not null; a return counts in the month corresponding to the returned_at timestamp's date (use its year-month).; Limit return counting to returned_at dates occurring in 2020 and months after January 2020 (i.e., 2020-02 through 2020-12).; Only include users who appear in USERS or ORDERS tables and who are in the cohort defined above.; If cohort_size is zero, return zero or null proportions explicitly to avoid division by zero.
Sort/limit: order by month ascending; no row limit

Use cohort_users_jan_first_purchase (one row per user) as the cohort source. 
Aggregate ORDERS by user and returned-month first: join ORDERS to cohort on ORDERS.user_id = cohort.user_id, filter ORDERS.returned_at IS NOT NULL and returned_at date in 2020-02..2020-12, compute returned_month = strftime('%Y-%m', datetime(returned_at/1000, 'unixepoch')) (or appropriate epoch conversion). 
From that filtered orders set, produce one row per cohort user per returned_month by grouping on user_id and returned_month (COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) >0 as flag) — then count distinct users per month.
Compute cohort_size as COUNT(DISTINCT cohort.user_id) from cohort_users_jan_first_purchase.
Final projection: month (YYYY-MM) for 2020-02..2020-12 (generate months via a months table or VALUES and left join counts), cohort_size, users_with_return_in_month, return_proportion = users_with_return_in_month / NULLIF(cohort_size,0).
Order by month ascending; no limit.

rows.question: Please generate a report that, for each month in 2021, provides the number of orders, the number of unique purchasers, and the profit (calculated as the sum of product retail prices minus the sum of product costs), where the orders were placed during 2021 by users who registered in 2021 for inventory items created in 2021, and group the results by the users' country, product department, and product category.
rows.rewrite:
Task: For each month of 2021, compute the number of orders, the number of unique purchasers, and the profit (sum of product retail prices minus sum of product costs) for orders placed in 2021 that meet these conditions: the ordering user registered in 2021 and the ordered inventory items were created in 2021; group the results by the user's country, the product department, and the product category.

Filters: Only include orders with ORDERS.created_at within the calendar year 2021 (i.e., timestamps corresponding to 2021-01-01 00:00:00 through 2021-12-31 23:59:59).; Only include orders where the ordering user (USERS.created_at) registered in 2021 (USERS.created_at within 2021-01-01 through 2021-12-31).; Only include order items whose related inventory item (INVENTORY_ITEMS.created_at) was created in 2021 (INVENTORY_ITEMS.created_at within 2021-01-01 through 2021-12-31).; Relate tables via: ORDERS.order_id = ORDER_ITEMS.order_id; ORDER_ITEMS.inventory_item_id = INVENTORY_ITEMS.id; ORDER_ITEMS.product_id = PRODUCTS.id (or INVENTORY_ITEMS.product_id), and ORDERS.user_id = USERS.id.; When computing product retail price and product cost for profit, use the retail price and cost from INVENTORY_ITEMS if available (INVENTORY_ITEMS.product_retail_price and INVENTORY_ITEMS.cost); otherwise use PRODUCTS.retail_price and PRODUCTS.cost. Sum retail prices and costs across included order items.; Include only data where all joining keys exist (i.e., ignore order items without matching inventory item or user or product), so that country, product_department and product_category are non-null.; Group results by month (based on ORDERS.created_at truncated to month), USERS.country, product_department and product_category.
Sort/limit: Order the results by year_month ascending, then by country ascending, then by product_department ascending, then by product_category ascending; no row limit.

- Use orders_core_2021_cohort (one row per order) joined to users_registration_ym on orders_core_2021_cohort.user_id = users_registration_ym.user_id; filter orders_core_2021_cohort.order_year = 2021 and users_registration_ym.user_created_year = 2021 to enforce order and user registration in 2021. JOIN-SAFETY: orders_core_2021_cohort grain order_id, users_registration_ym grain user_id — safe to join 1:1/ many-to-1 on user_id.
- Join ORDER_ITEMS to orders_core_2021_cohort on ORDER_ITEMS.order_id = orders_core_2021_cohort.order_id; before joining INVENTORY_ITEMS/Product measures, treat ORDER_ITEMS as the detail rows to aggregate (one row per order item). Do not join INVENTORY_ITEMS one-to-many without re-aggregation.

  FROM monthly_profits
  GROUP BY delivery_month
) p
  ON m.month = p.delivery_month
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT delivery_month, SUM(profit) AS profit
  FROM monthly_profits
  GROUP BY delivery_month
) p_prev
  ON TO_CHAR(ADD_MONTHS(TO_DATE(m.month || '-01','YYYY-MM-DD'), -1), 'YYYY-MM') = p_prev.delivery_month
ORDER BY month_over_month_increase DESC
LIMIT 5
